reasoning: This is a generic error handling workflow that serves as infrastructure for the entire automation system. The 'Error Trigger' node catches failures from any workflow in the system, then sends detailed error notifications via Gmail to 'dlschoolautomations@gmail.com'. The email template includes workflow name, execution URL, error message, stack trace, and last executed node - providing comprehensive debugging information. The 15% error rate across 40 executions suggests this is actively catching failures from other workflows. The 38 version iterations indicate ongoing refinement of error handling. The project context 'FairTix Automations' suggests this supports a ticketing platform's automation infrastructure.
name: System-Wide Error Notification Handler
businessNarrative: This workflow serves as the central nervous system for FairTix's automation infrastructure, automatically detecting and reporting failures across all automated processes. When any workflow in their system fails, this immediately sends detailed error reports to the operations team, enabling rapid response to issues that could affect ticket sales, customer communications, or event management. The comprehensive error details (stack traces, execution URLs, failed nodes) suggest a mature DevOps approach to automation reliability. With 40 executions and 15% error rate, this reveals the company is actively managing automation failures rather than letting them go unnoticed.
trigger: Any workflow in the FairTix automation system encounters an unhandled error or exception
dataFlow: Receives error context data (workflow name, execution details, error messages, stack traces) from failed workflows and sends formatted email notifications to operations team

detectability.evidence: No error handling or retry logic configured on the Gmail node - if email sending fails, there's no fallback notification mechanism
